steps.text: Stir balsamic vinegar, lemon juice, and soy sauce with salt, brown sugar, ground ginger, paprika, pepper, and red pepper flakes until the salt has dissolved. Stir in garlic, green onions, sesame oil, and peanut oil until well combined.
Pour marinade into a resealable plastic bag or glass bowl. Add salmon to marinade and gently toss to coat. Place into refrigerator and marinate 2 to 24 hours.
Prepare an outdoor grill for medium-high heat.
Drain excess marinade from salmon fillets. Grill until firm and opaque, about 4 minutes per side.

raw_recipe.headline: Slammin' Salmon
raw_recipe.description: This easy grilled slammin' salmon dish is packed full of Asian flavors! The salmon is slowly marinated to perfection and full of flavor for all to enjoy.
raw_recipe.name: Slammin' Salmon

review.reviewBody: Marinated for 10 hours in the fridge inside of a gallon zippie bag. I used sesame seeds - no oil at all. I didn't grill, but instead baked covered at 400 degrees for 10 minutes or until fork flaky and cooked all the way through. I did use the marinade for a reduction sauce (served under the salmon on the plate). I placed the marinade in a sauce pan for about 15 minutes, adding a bit of white wine to enhance the flavor. A huge hit with the entire family!!

Slammin is right! I marinated for about 8 hours. I omitted the peanut oil because I didn’t have any. And substituted the ground ginger for about 2 tbsp of fresh ginger because it’s what I had on hand. I then put it in my NuWave air fryer oven at 350 for 30 minutes. It came out perfect! Will definitely be using it again.

This was outstanding. We loved it and can’t wait until we’re able to entertain again and can offer this!!! I did use the sesame oil but not the peanut oil. Marinated in a baggie for about 5 hrs. Took Ingrams recommendations - baked it in the oven at 400 for 10-12 min and reduced the marinade to serve as a sauce.

FANTASTIC marinade. Followed recipe exactly, was delicious and super easy to pull together. Marinated for 24 hours. Thank you reviewers for all the great tips. I did save the marinade and cooked it with some white wine. At the end I added some black beans and corn. I turned this salmon dish into a salad and served everything on spring greens with additional green onions, chopped cilantro, jalapeños and chopped unsalted peanuts. I small dash of vinaigrette at the end to balance out all flavors. The salad was ah-mazing. Hub’s said this recipe is a keeper and I couldn’t agree more. Cheers

My new favorite salmon recipe! I fish in Alaska every summer, I have a freezer full of salmon filets, so we eat a lot of it, this was the best recipe so far. I made a double batch of marinade to accommodate more fish, I might use just a little less lemon next time. Just before cooking it I took a small sieve and scooped out onions and some of the spices out of the marinade and put it on top of the filets before grilling...glad I did, YUM! My filets are a little thicker than the usual farm salmon, so I grilled it for 5 minutes on each side...perfect. Just a little bit of kick, but not too much, and not enough to mask the true flavor of the salmon...I'm going to try this on other varieties of fish too.

Delicious!!! I used olive oil because I didn't have any peanut and I only marinated about an hour and a half. Baked in the oven and reduced the marinade to make a sauce. I will definitely make this again soon!

Very good! Marinated 2 hrs., grilled on my Ninja Air Fryer, med high grill setting, skin side down 5 minutes then set to air crisp 2 minutes. No need to turn over. BTW when I lived in Talkeetna AK there was a band named Slammin Salmon that sometimes played at the Fairview Inn...great music and great recipe.

This is the second time I am making this. The first time I used Salmon in a cast iron pan & cooked it on the gas stove top. Tonight I am using Steelhead Trout & following the recipe exactly. I put the fish & sauce in the fridge overnight (approx. 12 hours. I will use a 1/2 cup of Pinot Grigio to reduce the sauce and make a glaze. I plan to serve this with garlic red potatoes & Brussel sprouts with bacon. I am bringing this meal to a friend tonight that HATES fish & I am betting it will turn her around (fingers crossed). This recipe is awesome!

Served this at a summer dinner party and got raves all around. Marinated for 5 hours, which was perfect. Every guest requested the recipe. I like the idea of reducing and serving the sauce. Such a shame to waste the marinade.

I followed the recipe exactly but I cut down the peanut oil to just a few tablespoons and it was fabulous. I also cooked it in an air fryer. Huge hit and will make it again and again. Going to try it with chicken and pork too.

Incredible salmon - I followed the recipe spices specifically but changed out the peanut oil to olive oil and skilled the sesame oil, and it was still delicious. I may try 1 tablespoon of peanut butter next time to give it that peanut butter flare, as mentioned in a previous review. I also marinated it for 30 minutes. I baked mine at 400 degrees for 25 minutes (was thick salmon) with skin down, and drizzled the remaining marinade on top. It's the best I've ever had and will make this for years to come. Thanks for sharing this recipe. :)
Tested like teriyaki which is ok but I expected more
I make this all the time Every time I serve it I have to give out the recipe. It’s great another thing I like about it it can sit in fridge for 24 hours and it’s wonderful
Excellent! Going for it again, but with a bit more 🌶️. I didn't have peanut oil so I used olive oil, but I'm going to buy peanut oil and check it out! Easy, convenient, and delicious! 🤤Thank you!!

This is my husband’s favorite way to eat his favorite fish. It’s definitely spicy, but not over the top. I saw another rating that mentioned doing a sauce reduction with the marinade. I’m going to try that rather than pour those lovely spices down the sink! And I may try baking it as well, although I hate to mess with a good thing!
I've made several times and everyone loved it.
This tasted good. It has a lot of ingredients though, almost too many. I marinated for an hour and it was still very flavorful. I would not marinate longer than a few hours.
Absolutely Not, didn't need any change.
Disappointed. Was looking forward to this with all of the positive reviews. Didn't taste asian. All I tasted was the sour balsamic vinegar.
